article.title: Put off
article.description: Meaning: to postpone or delay something. Example: 'We had to put off the meeting until next week.' Grammar note: separable — 'put the meeting off' is also correct. Second meaning: to make someone dislike something — 'The bad reviews put me off that restaurant.'
article.content: Meaning: to postpone or delay something. Example: 'We had to put off the meeting until next week.' Grammar note: separable — 'put the meeting off' is also correct. Second meaning: to make someone dislike something — 'The bad reviews put me off that restaurant.'

generated.caption:
Ever said "I need to put it off" and wondered if you used it right? 🤔

"Put off" has two main uses! It can mean to **postpone or delay** something, like: "We had to put off the meeting until next week."

It can also mean to **make someone dislike** something: "The bad reviews put me off that restaurant."

Save this tip for later! Follow @TheEnglishVault for daily English boosts!
generated.script:
"Put off" sunke thoda confusion hota hai na? Ya isko galat use kar dete ho kabhi-kabhi?

"Put off" ke do main meanings hain. Pehla, to postpone ya delay something. Jaise, 'We had to put off the meeting until next week.' Matlab, meeting agle hafte tak postpone karni padi. Aur haan, yeh separable hai, 'put the meeting off' bhi sahi hai. Dusra meaning hai, to make someone dislike something. For example, 'The bad reviews put me off that restaurant.' Matlab, un reviews ne mujhe us restaurant se door kar diya.

Toh next time jab koi cheez postpone karni ho, ya kisi cheez se dislike ho jaaye, toh "put off" use karna. Ab samajh aaya?

Comment mein batao, aapko ye dono meanings pata the ya nahi!

slides.body: The phrasal verb 'put off' has two main uses in English. Firstly, it means to postpone or delay something. For example, 'We had to put off the meeting until next week' because of scheduling conflicts. Remember, it's separable, so 'We had to put the meeting off' is also perfectly correct. Secondly, 'put off' can mean to make someone dislike something or lose interest in it. If a restaurant has 'bad reviews, they might put you off that restaurant' entirely. It's important to understand both contexts to use this common phrasal verb correctly.
